report:
### Conclusion
**Supported.** Opening a bedroom window or internal door generally improves sleep quality by increasing ventilation and lowering indoor carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) concentrations.

### Key Evidence
* **Reduced $\text{CO}_2$ Accumulation:** In closed, poorly ventilated bedrooms, exhaled $\text{CO}_2$ accumulates overnight. Opening a window or door increases air exchange, keeping $\text{CO}_2$ levels lower.
* **Enhanced Sleep Efficiency:** Controlled studies using actigraphy and physiological monitoring show that lower overnight $\text{CO}_2$ levels correlate with fewer awakenings, greater sleep depth, and improved overall sleep efficiency.
* **Next-Day Cognitive Benefits:** Better nighttime ventilation is associated with decreased morning sleepiness, improved concentration, and better performance on cognitive tasks the following day.

### Caveats
Although airflow improves sleep, external disturbances—such as traffic noise, extreme outdoor temperatures, ambient light, draft, or outdoor allergens—can counteract these benefits if environmental conditions outside are unfavorable.

### Sources
* PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26452168/
* Technical University of Denmark: https://www.dtu.dk/english/newsarchive/2023/05/ventilate-your-bedroom-at-night-you-perform-better-the-next-day
* HU University of Applied Sciences Utrecht: https://www.hu.nl/onderzoek/publicaties/windowdoor-openingmediated-bedroom-ventilation-and-its-impact-on-sleep-quality-of-healthy-young
* Medical Xpress: https://medicalxpress.com/news/2025-10-exploring-effect-bedroom-ventilation-quality.html
